# Convex-potential capacity duality and actual affine-contact transport

This note gives an exact restriction on a prescribed finite cap profile on
common-normal simplex fibers. It does not prove the selected-circuit
Gamma bound. Unlike a fixed old-marginal transport calculation, the
restriction applies to the actual, possibly deformed boundary measures.

## 1. A capacity form of convex order, with proof

Let mu and nu be finite nonnegative Borel measures of compact support in
R^D. The following statements are equivalent.

(a) For every finite continuous nonnegative convex function phi on R^D,

    integral phi d mu <= integral phi d nu.                    (1)

(b) There is a finite nonnegative measure pi on R^D times R^D with
first marginal mu, second marginal nu'<=nu, and the barycenter property

    integral h(x)(y-x) d pi(x,y)=0                             (2)

for every continuous scalar function h on R^D.
Equivalently, the conditional law pi_x of y given x has mean x for
mu-almost every x. If mu=0, the zero measure is allowed.

The use of a SUBmeasure nu' is essential: the constant test only requires
mu(R^D)<=nu(R^D), not equality. No artificial point or unrecorded mass is
introduced into the final certificate.

Proof of (b)=>(a). Conditional Jensen gives phi(x)<=integral phi(y)d pi_x.
Integrate, then use phi>=0 and nu'<=nu. Compact supports make all integrals
finite.

First prove the other direction for finite atomic measures
mu=sum_i m_i delta_(x_i), nu=sum_j n_j delta_(y_j), with positive masses.
The desired variables p_ij satisfy

    p_ij>=0, sum_j p_ij=m_i,
    sum_j p_ij(y_j-x_i)=0, sum_i p_ij<=n_j.                    (3)

Here is the finite separation argument, including signs. If (3) is
infeasible, separation from the finitely generated feasibility cone gives
numbers alpha_i, vectors h_i, and beta_j>=0 such that

    alpha_i+h_i dot(y_j-x_i)<=beta_j for every i,j,
    sum_i m_i alpha_i > sum_j n_j beta_j.                     (4)

Indeed add nonnegative unused-capacity variables s_j to make the last
constraints equalities. A separating linear functional nonnegative on
each variable column has coefficients (-alpha_i,-h_i,beta_j); its value
at the right-hand side is negative. Nonnegativity on the s_j columns is
exactly beta_j>=0, and on the p_ij columns is exactly the first inequality
in (4). A finitely generated cone is closed, so ordinary finite-dimensional
separation applies.

Set

    phi(v)=max(0, max_i[alpha_i+h_i dot(v-x_i)]).

This is a finite continuous nonnegative convex function,
phi(x_i)>=alpha_i, and phi(y_j)<=beta_j. Thus (4) contradicts (1).
This proves finite feasibility.

For general compact measures, use cubic grids of mesh tending to zero.
Partition the source support by finitely many half-open grid cubes and
replace each nonzero cell measure by its mass at its conditional mean;
call the finite measure mu_N. Jensen proves mu_N<=_cx mu. Its support is
within the cell diameter of the original support, and mu_N converges
weakly to mu by uniform continuity of continuous tests on a fixed box.

For the target, represent every point of a grid cube by the usual product
barycentric weights at that cube's 2^D vertices. These weights are
nonnegative, sum to one, and have that point as their mean. Integrating
them against nu gives a finite atomic measure nu_N. Jensen proves
nu<=_cx nu_N. The vertices lie within a grid-cell diameter of the original
support, and nu_N converges weakly to nu. Half-open cell conventions make
all choices Borel and count boundary points once.

Consequently, for every test in (1),

    integral phi d mu_N <= integral phi d mu
       <= integral phi d nu <= integral phi d nu_N.

The finite result gives pi_N with first marginal mu_N, second marginal
at most nu_N, and (2). All pi_N have the same finite mass and support in
a fixed compact product box. Weak compactness of finite measures on a
compact metric space gives a convergent subsequence pi_N -> pi. Marginal
convergence gives its first marginal mu. Testing the second marginal
against nonnegative continuous functions and passing to the limit gives
nu'<=nu. The functions h(x)(y-x) are continuous and bounded on the fixed
box, so (2) passes to the limit. Continuous h determine the signed vector
measure obtained by integrating y-x over source sets; hence its vanishing
is equivalent to the conditional-mean assertion. This proves (b).

Only auxiliary finite measures were approximated. No convex body, cap,
boundary trace, normal, or critical point was approximated. The final
transport is supported on the original compact supports because its two
marginals are mu and a submeasure of nu.

## 2. Exact application to a finite-normal boundary profile

Let P be a finite set of actual positive-volume mixed fibers in
R^n times R^d, d>=1. Suppose the fibers are common-normal simplexes

    K_z={x:lambda_i(x)>=b_i(z), 0<=i<=d},
    sum_i lambda_i=1, r_z=1-sum_i b_i(z)>0.                    (5)

The lambda_i are fixed affine barycentric coordinate functions. Let F_i(z)
be the actual facet lambda_i=b_i(z), and let n_i be its outward unit
normal. Define the fixed-normal measure

    eta_i=sum_(z in P) delta_z times H_(d-1)|F_i(z).           (6)

For d=1 this is counting measure on the corresponding endpoints. In
higher dimensions intersections of facets have zero H_(d-1) measure.
The normal bundle measure is the sum of (6), with n_i attached.

Let W be any bounded nonnegative Borel function on that bundle, in
particular an actual finite weighted profile of CLOSED ambient caps.
Define its efficiency as the supremum of integral Phi W / integral Phi
over continuous nonnegative potentials which, for each fixed normal,
are finite convex functions of the physical coordinates (z,x), with a
positive denominator. Let c>=0. Because the normals are finitely many
and distinct, continuous nonnegative normal selectors isolate each n_i.
Therefore efficiency <=c is equivalent to

    integral phi (W-c) d eta_i<=0                             (7)

for every i and every finite continuous nonnegative convex physical phi.
One direction follows by selectors. Conversely apply (7) to each
restriction Phi(n_i,.,.) and add; no interchange of supremum and integral
is needed.

Define actual positive and negative excess measures

    mu_i=(W-c)_+ eta_i, nu_i=(c-W)_+ eta_i.                    (8)

By Section1, (7) is equivalent to a barycentric transport pi_i from mu_i
to an actual submeasure nu_i'<=nu_i. It follows that an efficiency upper
bound has an exact certificate preserving BOTH the integer base mean and
the continuous physical mean, with all unused negative capacity retained.
These are the current measures (8), not old measures from an undeformed
body. Boundary mass in W is included in (8) without alteration.

## 3. Every transition preserves actual affine contact

Convex compatibility of the fibers implies the sampled Jensen condition

    b_i(p)<=sum_z t_z b_i(z)
    whenever p=sum_z t_z z, t_z>=0, sum_z t_z=1.               (9)

For example, convex combinations of the endpoint fibers lie in K_p;
taking the minimum of lambda_i gives (9). Let

    G_i=conv{(z,b_i(z)):z in P}.

Every listed point lies on the lower convex hull. More intrinsically,
define on conv(P)

    bbar_i(v)=min{sum_z t_z b_i(z):sum_z t_z z=v,
                     sum_z t_z=1,t_z>=0}.

It is a finite convex polyhedral function and (9) gives bbar_i(p)=b_i(p).
There is no need to assume differentiability of an underlying body.

Take a conditional transition of pi_i at source X=(p,x) in F_i(p).
Let t_z be its target base probabilities. Its physical barycenter gives

    p=sum_z t_z z,
    b_i(p)=lambda_i(x)=sum_z t_z b_i(z).                       (10)

Thus (9) is equality at EVERY transition, not just after integrating over
sources. Equivalently, if M_i(p) is the minimal face of G_i containing
(p,b_i(p)), then all target bases satisfy

    (z,b_i(z)) in M_i(p).                                     (11)

To see this without any strict-convexity claim, the barycenter of the
finitely many lifted base points is the source graph point. Any face
containing that point contains every positive term in such a convex
representation. Intersect all such faces. Conversely any representation
within this face which has mean p automatically has the required graph
coordinate; (11) is a necessary support restriction, not sufficient for
the remaining continuous barycenter or the capacity constraints.

On the convex hull of the positively used bases, bbar_i is affine. For a
short proof, if p=sum t_z z with positive t_z and equality in (10), take
any v=sum s_z z, choose epsilon>0 with t_z-epsilon s_z>=0, and write
p=epsilon v+(1-epsilon)w. Applying convexity twice forces
bbar_i(v)=sum s_z b_i(z). This is exact anchored Jensen equality.

There is a stronger simultaneous statement at any source point where
additional actual fiber constraints are active. If
lambda_l(x)=b_l(p) for l in a set J containing i, physical barycenters and
fiber inequalities give

    b_l(p)=integral lambda_l(x') d pi_(i,X)
       >=sum_z t_z b_l(z)>=b_l(p).

All inequalities are equalities. Hence every target point has
lambda_l(x')=b_l(z) for every l in J, and all target bases lie in the
intersection of the corresponding minimal-face index sets. At a fiber
vertex of type j, J consists of the d indices l!=j; target points must
then be the SAME vertex type j. This recovers the exact simultaneous
contact relation proved in the companion contact-rigidity source, now
for every existing transport transition. It does not pretend that
vertices carry positive facet measure when d>=2.

## 4. Face capacities and the precise sense of cellwise decomposition

For a face F of G_i set

    P_F={z:(z,b_i(z)) in F},
    E_F=union_(z in P_F)({z} times F_i(z)).

If a source base lies in P_F, its minimal face is contained in F. Thus
(11) shows pi_i sends that source only to E_F. The actual target capacity
therefore implies

    mu_i(E_F)<=nu_i(E_F),
    integral_(E_F) W d eta_i<=c eta_i(E_F).                   (12)

This is a necessary actual facet-mass quota, not an integer parity quota.
It retains the current facet sizes and cap traces.

The decomposition is naturally along a FINITE FACE POSET. A source with
minimal face F can send to bases whose minimal faces are subfaces of F.
Two different source cells may share destination capacity on their common
subfaces. One cannot partition the certificate into independent affine
cells and reuse that capacity. The global inequalities nu_i'<=nu_i in
Section2 remain in force.

When F is an exposed lower face, choose an affine a on base space with
b_i(z)>=a(z), equality exactly for z in P_F. Since P is finite, the
positive gaps outside P_F have a positive minimum. For smaller delta,

    Phi(n,z,x)=psi_i(n)[delta+a(z)-lambda_i(x)]_+               (13)

is exactly delta on E_F and zero on all other actual normal-bundle
facets. Thus (12) is also detected by an explicit admissible potential.
Only uniform localization on the whole fixed-normal facets is asserted.
An arbitrary relative-interior point of a facet is not thereby exposed.

If every graph point is a vertex of G_i, (11) forces base-preserving
transport for that normal. This conclusion does not follow merely from
nonaffinity of b_i: a lower face may contain many actual bases and can
have full dimension n. Accordingly this note gives no automatic strict
reduction of the number of fibers or of integer dimension.

## 5. Exact shared-subface example

The shared-capacity warning occurs in an actual compatible simplex
family. Take P={-2,-1,0,1,2}, d=2, 0<epsilon<1/2, and

    b_0(z)=epsilon |z|, b_1(z)=b_2(z)=0.

These are the fibers of the convex set described by these inequalities
and -2<=z<=2. Put

    X_z=(z; lambda_0=epsilon|z|,
             lambda_1=lambda_2=(1-epsilon|z|)/2).

Every X_z lies on the relative interior of actual facet0. The measures

    mu=delta_(X_-1)+delta_(X_1),
    nu=(1/2)delta_(X_-2)+delta_(X_0)+(1/2)delta_(X_2)

have the exact barycentric certificate

    X_-1 -> (X_-2+X_0)/2,
    X_1  -> (X_0+X_2)/2.

The two maximal affine lower faces have base intervals [-2,0] and [0,2].
Both transports consume the SAME target atom at X_0, one half each. This
is an illustration of the geometric/capacity issue, not a claim that
these atomic measures equal excess measures of a genuine critical cap
profile. It rules out disjoint-cell reasoning even in actual compatible
fiber geometry.

## 6. What this adds to the selected-circuit problem

For any prescribed actual circuit, a claimed upper bound below Gamma has
to supply the exact transports of Sections2--3 for its actual excess
measures. Those transports can use only common affine-contact regions,
and must respect all face capacities simultaneously. A newly exposed
high-profile bundle point instead gives the explicit paying hinge from
the companion contact-rigidity source.

Neither direction proves that an arbitrary deepest source has a paying
SELECTED circuit. A product has affine support offsets, so its maximal
contact face contains all bases; there is no induction progress from
(11) alone. More generally full-dimensional affine contact cells and
shared lower-face capacities remain possible. Actual criticality,
lattice completeness, and favorable selection must enter any further
step; they were not needed or inferred in this exact transport theorem.
